01 / What the data show

TE families leave distinct signatures across RNA biology.

Long-read transcript models help connect repetitive sequences to the exact regulatory and RNA features they overlap.

FINDING 01cis-regulatory elements

Enhancer-like tCREs are enriched for TE overlap.

More than one in five tCREs overlap TEs. Enrichment varies by cell type and TE family, with enhancer-like tCREs enriched and promoter-like tCREs depleted.

Family-level enrichment in enhancers · log₂ odds ratio · Fisher’s exact test, BH-FDR
TE ENRICHMENTtCREs

Transposons light up enhancers and avoid promoters.

Each row compares one TE family in enhancer-like and promoter-like tCREs. The x-position shows log₂ odds ratio versus other CREs: most families shift toward enrichment in enhancer-like tCREs and depletion in promoter-like tCREs.

Pink: enhancer-like · blue: promoter-like · filled dots: FDR < 0.05 · arrows connect promoter-like to enhancer-like estimates
FINDING 02splice junctions

TE-overlapped junctions appear more often in non-coding genes.

TE-overlapped splice junctions are more common in non-coding than coding genes (odds ratios 5.4–27.4). Alu overlaps about 9.9% of non-coding acceptor sites; the plot also separates sense and antisense overlaps.

Acceptor (AG) and donor (GT) sites · coding vs non-coding genes
ORIENTATION MATTERSlncRNA splice sites

TE family shapes strand orientation.

Within lncRNAs, LTR-derived splice sites are mostly sense-oriented. SINE- and LINE-derived sites are mostly antisense-oriented.

Share of TE-overlapping splice sites by orientation and TE class
FINDING 03transcript termination

Termination motifs show a family-specific split.

The class-level plot compares the share of PAS hexamers and noPAS sites overlapped by each TE class, split by coding status and strand. LINE and LTR elements are more common among PAS hexamers, while SINEs dominate noPAS sites. The lncRNA family plot highlights more PAS hits for ERVL-MaLR and ERV1, and more noPAS hits for Alu.

WHY IT MATTERSTE-derived sequence may contribute directly to transcript processing signals, not only to regulatory DNA.
Class-level overlap percentages by coding status and strand. PAS: polyadenylation signal; noPAS: 25-nt window without the canonical hexamer.
Family-level lncRNA comparison: top TE families associated with PAS versus noPAS sites; bubble size shows hit count, bars show sense/antisense share, with FDR-adjusted enrichment.
02 / Study design

Full-length reads resolve what short reads blur.

Transposable elements repeat across the genome. Capturing full transcript molecules makes it possible to map those sequences within transcript models and connect them to TSSs, splice junctions and termination motifs.

CFC-seq: cap-trapping, poly(A)-tailing and long-read sequencing
01

Build full-length transcript models

CFC-seq data from HEK cells, THP1 series and neuron series.

02

Annotate genomic repeats

RepeatMasker annotations on the hg38 reference genome.

03

Define cell-specific tCREs

Transcribed cis-regulatory elements defined from cell-type-specific transcription start sites.

04

Test enrichment and overlap

Compare TE classes and families across regulatory and RNA features; assess enrichment with Fisher’s exact test and FDR correction.

03 / The bigger question

What if some “genomic leftovers” are working parts of the transcriptome?

The results suggest that transposable elements can act as modular building blocks in human RNA regulation and architecture.

04 / Takeaway

TEs contribute to both regulatory DNA and RNA structure.

  • Full-length long-read models support unambiguous mapping of TE-derived sequences.
  • TEs overlap enhancer-like tCREs more often, with cell-type-specific patterns.
  • TEs contribute to splice junctions and polyadenylation-related motifs, with family-specific orientation and enrichment patterns.
